# `project.reproduction.pipelines`

[project](../../README.md) · [reproduction](../README.md) · pipelines

THE TWO PIPELINES, and the only place a reader of a day-zero bundle learns there are two. A bundle may declare a DATA pipeline and an ONTOLOGY pipeline, each with its own MANUALLY STARTED entry point, and the data pipeline's `exit` is not a produces-glob but A NAMED HUMAN'S SIGN-OFF. That one line is the whole governance ruling made checkable: the ontology pipeline may not start until a person has approved the dataset configuration. WHY A CORE KEY AND NOT AN EXTENSION: `^x-` was CLOSED in v0.1.14 and check_extension_keys refuses it as MAC012, and the measured lesson is exactly this case — x-grain held the grain, was unreachable by every gate, and two of four declarations rotted into false while still reading as VERIFIED. A declaration no gate can reach is worse than none. ADDITIVE AND OPTIONAL: a manifest without this key declares one pipeline, the two-pipeline gate does not apply to it, and its ontology plane stays governed by the operator's unlock marker exactly as before — so no existing bundle turns red. EXACTLY TWO PROPERTIES, additionalProperties false: a THIRD pipeline is then a schema change, which is a decision with a record, rather than a config value somebody adds on a Tuesday. Read by tools/check_data_plane_approved.py and by the ontology guard.

> **2 keys at this level carry no description in `mac.schema.json`.** The place to fix one is the schema, which is its one home; this page is generated and cannot hold the answer.
